summary: 戈雅从挂毯草图中练就对人物和光线的把握，后来在宫廷与私人肖像之间形成独特画风。他既留意人物所处的空间与身份，也尽量呈现自己实际看到的个体。

paragraphs.brief: 在任何其他伟大的肖像家的工作中，没有一个民族、民间传统和迷信如此全面和无情地被俘虏。
sentences: There are, according to current scholarship, 160 existing portraits by Francisco de Goya, about a third of his painted output.
根据目前的奖学金，Francisco de Goya现有160幅肖像画，约占其绘画产出的三分之一。
The real number, though, is much greater, since there are no pure landscapes in Goya's work.
不过，实际数字要大得多，因为戈亚的工作没有纯净的景观。
He was not interested in paintings of nature – everything he ever did deals with people.
他对大自然的绘画不感兴趣他和人的一切交易
In the work of no other great portraitist are a nation's people, folk traditions and superstitions so comprehensively and relentlessly captured.
在任何其他伟大的肖像家的工作中，没有一个民族、民间传统和迷信如此全面和无情地被俘虏。
Put his work together – the public and private paintings and the personal drawings and sketches – and what you have is a comprehensive portrait of Spain itself.
将他的作品 — — 公共和私人绘画以及个人绘画和素描 — — 以及你拥有的西班牙本身的全面肖像。
His subject was a good one since Goya lived in fascinating times: his lifetime was a period that saw Spain pass through enormous changes.
戈亚在迷人的时代生活，他的主题是一个很好的主题：他的一生是西班牙经历巨大变化的时期。
People were the constant during these unstable times and he recorded both the faces of those who mattered to Spain and to him – often they were one and the same.
在这种不稳定的时期，人们是常态的，他记录了对西班牙和他都很重要的人的面孔——他们往往是同一个人。

paragraphs.brief: 他作为肖像师的工作源自他于1775年搬到马德里皇家塔佩斯特工厂后为该工厂画的45幅挂毯漫画。
sentences: His work as a portraitist has its origins in the 45 tapestry cartoons he painted for the Royal Tapestry Factory in Madrid after he moved there in 1775.
他作为肖像师的工作源自他于1775年搬到马德里皇家塔佩斯特工厂后为该工厂画的45幅挂毯漫画。

Although his designs don't show portraits, they do show types of people – the residents of the city who gave Madrid its street swagger: peasants and rich men, courting couples, singers, hunters, children and young men and women playing blind man's buff or tossing a mannequin into the air.
虽然他的设计没有显示肖像，但确实展示了人们的类型 — — 给马德里街头打滚的城市居民：农民和富人、情侣、歌手、猎人、儿童、青年男女玩弄盲人的马屁或把假发扔到空中。
The pictures use a limited range of colours, and the faces are individualised without being those of particular people.
图片使用范围有限的颜色，脸部被个性化，没有特定的人。
But in them Goya practised poses and groupings and a way of handling light on and around figures that was to be invaluable.
但戈亚在他们中表现了姿势和组合，以及处理数字的亮度和周围情况的方法，这是非常宝贵的。

paragraphs.brief: 挂毯的设计显示了社会角色而不是居住着他们的人但是当它要画肖像的时候戈亚会把这个挂在头上
sentences: The tapestry designs show social roles rather than the people inhabiting them, but when it came to painting portraits, Goya would turn this on its head.
挂毯的设计显示了社会角色而不是居住着他们的人但是当它要画肖像的时候戈亚会把这个挂在头上

His greatest strength as a portraitist is that regardless of the status of the sitter, be they a king or a queen, a soldier, a priest or writer, it was the person he showed first and their position second.
他作为肖像师的最大力量是不管保姆的身份如何不管是国王还是女王士兵牧师还是作家

It was this trait, most apparent in his royal portraiture, which has led him to be seen as satirising the Bourbon monarchy rather than as a painter who depicted what he saw without using the usual flattering conventions.
正是这种特征，最明显的是他的王室肖像，使他被视为使波旁君主制感到满足，而不是一个画家，他没有使用通常的恭维习俗来描述他所看到的。
In the art critic Robert Hughes's phrase he did not 'pay reflexive homage to authority' but instead walked a fine line between respect and truth.
在艺术评论家罗伯特·休斯的话说，他并没有“对权威的反射式敬意”，而是在尊重与真理之间走过一条细线。

paragraphs.brief: 戈亚成功得很快：1785年，他成为皇家学院的画部副校长(他给学生的主要信息是颠覆性的)，1786年，他成为正式的法庭画家，这涉及到画“皇家服务所需的作品”。
sentences: Goya's success was rapid: in 1785 he was made deputy director of painting at the Royal Academy (his main message to his students was subversive – 'there are no rules in painting') and in 1786 he became the official court painter, which involved painting 'works required for royal service'.
戈亚成功得很快：1785年，他成为皇家学院的画部副校长(他给学生的主要信息是颠覆性的)，1786年，他成为正式的法庭画家，这涉及到画“皇家服务所需的作品”。
He immediately spent some of his generous salary on a two-wheeled horse carriage (one of only three in Madrid at the time) which he crashed on his first outing.
他立即将他的一些丰厚工资花在一辆两轮马车上(当时只有三辆马车之一在马德里)，他在第一次出行时坠毁。

His self-confidence untouched, he wrote to his childhood friend Martin Zapater: “I have now established an enviable way of living: I do not wait on anyone in antechambers, and if anyone wants anything from me they must come to me.
他没有自信地写信给他童年的朋友马丁·萨帕特尔：“我现在建立了一种令人羡慕的生活方式：我不等待任何有技术的人，如果有人想从我这里得到什么，他们必须来找我。
I have made myself more in demand and unless it is a person of rank or at the request of a friend I would do nothing for anyone...”
我让自己更需要除非是位高贵的人或者应朋友的要求我什么都不会为任何人做...

paragraphs.brief: 他成功的原因之一是，与18世纪的英国艺术家Gainsborough不同，他并不痛恨肖像在经济上是必要的工作，在他可以专注于更高艺术的时候，这种工作就被吃掉了。
sentences: Part of the reason for his success was that, unlike the 18th-century British artist Gainsborough, for example, he did not resent portraiture as an economically necessary chore that ate away at the time he could devote to higher art.
他成功的原因之一是，与18世纪的英国艺术家Gainsborough不同，他并不痛恨肖像在经济上是必要的工作，在他可以专注于更高艺术的时候，这种工作就被吃掉了。
Portraiture fascinated him; it was, as he put it, part of that 'sacred science which requires so much study', and his portraits reveal a fully engaged artist.
肖像令他着迷；正如他所说，这是“神圣的科学需要大量研究”的一部分，他的肖像展示了一位完全投入其中的艺术家。
There is hardly any repetition in his poses (he drew on prints of English portraits for inspiration).
几乎没有人重复他的表情(他用英文肖像的指纹来启发人们)。
He worked hard to give his sitters in repose a sense of latent movement and he defined them by the careful depiction of the space around them.
他辛勤工作，让坐坐者重新感觉潜伏运动，他仔细地描述周围的空间，以此来界定他们。

paragraphs.brief: 我的艺术揭示了理想主义和真理，戈亚声称。
sentences: “My work is very simple.
“我的工作非常简单。
My art reveals idealism and truth,” Goya claimed.
我的艺术揭示了理想主义和真理，戈亚声称。
The truth, though is always more apparent than the idealism.
真相，虽然总是比理想主义更明显。

With the portrait of Charles IV and the royal family of 1800, one of the most important commissions of his career, Goya rejected entirely the grandeur of majesty to portray the assembled Bourbons as they appeared – a motley grouping in fancy clothes.
戈亚以查尔斯四世和皇室1800年的肖像... ...他的职业生涯中最重要的委员会之一... ...完全拒绝皇上，穿着花哨衣服的摩特利。
In fact, a French visitor to the Spanish court had previously likened Charles and his queen Maria Luisa to a butcher and his wife.
事实上，一位法国游客曾到过西班牙法庭，把查尔斯和他的女王玛丽亚·路易莎比作一个屠夫和他的妻子。
Goya may have been a political liberal but he wouldn't have jeopardised his hard-won new position as first court painter in order to score political points at the expense of his patrons.
戈亚可能是一个政治自由主义者但他不会为了赢得政治分数而损害他来之不易的新法庭画家的地位
That his sitters didn't regard the portrait as unflattering was evidenced by succeeding royal commissions, not least his 1815 portrait of Ferdinand VII.
他的坐席人并不认为画像是令人不快的由继承的皇家委员会证明特别是他的1815年的费迪南七世肖像
Ferdinand himself was physically unprepossessing, and had a reputation for being tyrannical, vicious and small-minded, so that is exactly how Goya shows him.
费迪南在身体上不占便宜并且以暴虐、恶毒和小心为名戈亚就是这么给他看的
The king, however, looking in Goya's particular mirror, saw no such characteristics staring back at him.
但是国王在戈亚的镜子里看不到他有这种特征

paragraphs.brief: 费尔南多的肖像与另一幅引人注目的作品形成对照，那是 1820 年戈雅与阿列塔医生的双人肖像。两者的对照从道德角度呈现了人类处境的三个侧面。
sentences: The private side of Goya's portraiture was a world away from the public.
戈亚画像的私人方面是一个远离公众的世界
The contrast between the Ferdinand portrait and the remarkable 1820 double portrait showing Goya with Dr Arrieta represents a moral version of three aspects of the human condition.
费尔南多的肖像与另一幅引人注目的作品形成对照，那是 1820 年戈雅与阿列塔医生的双人肖像。两者的对照从道德角度呈现了人类处境的三个侧面。
In this portrait, the 73-year-old painter is suffering from a debilitating illness and is being tended by his doctor.
在这幅肖像中，这位73岁的画家患有虚弱疾病，并接受医生的照顾。
If Ferdinand represents human malignity and Goya its frailty then Arrieta stands for man's innate kindness.
如果费迪南代表了人类的尊严戈亚代表了它的脆弱那么阿列塔代表了人类天生的善良

While not all his portraits are successful (some have a doll-like stiffness), this is what Goya at his best could do: in the guise of representing individuals he showed, without judging, man as a universal being.
虽然他的肖像并非都成功(有些人有像娃娃一样的僵硬性)，但戈亚最擅长的就是这样做：以他所展示的个人为幌子，不作评判，以人为世界性。

items.en: a reference to a weakness of some of Goya’s portraits
items.zh: 提到戈亚的一些肖像的弱点
items.why: 作者承认戈雅有些肖像像玩偶一样僵硬，正是作品的一个弱点。

items.en: a reason why some painters may not have enjoyed painting portraits
items.zh: 画家可能不喜欢画像的原因
items.why: 有的画家把肖像委托视作谋生所需的苦差，担心它占用追求更高艺术的时间。

items.en: a reference to a type of painting which Goya did not produce
items.zh: 提及戈亚没有生产的某类绘画
items.why: A段明确说明戈雅的作品里没有纯风景画，他的作品都关乎人。

items.en: a description of Goya’s reactions to a promotion
items.zh: 描述戈亚对一项宣传的反应
items.why: 升任宫廷画家后，戈雅马上用部分优厚薪水买了马车，随后又写信表达对新地位的自信。

items.en: a summary of the historical significance of Goya’s work
items.zh: 戈亚工作的历史意义摘要
items.why: 把公私绘画、素描与草图合起来，就得到一幅西班牙社会的整体肖像，点出作品的历史意义。

items.en: Which TWO of the following statements does the writer make about Goya's tapestry cartoons?
items.zh: 作者对戈亚的挂毯漫画做了以下哪些陈述？
correct: They show the lively Madrid people Goya had observed.
他们向马德里人展示了戈亚观察过的活泼。
Goya developed techniques in them which became useful to him later.
Goya开发了这些技术，这些技术后来对他有用。

items.en: Which TWO of the following statements does the writer make about Goya's approach to portrait painting?
items.zh: 作者对戈亚画肖像的方法做了以下两个陈述？
correct: He paid close attention to the background in his portraits.
他非常关注他的肖像中的背景。
He tried to avoid showing his subjects in similar poses.
他试图避免展示他的主体类似的姿势。

items.en: He received many similar ________ but this one was particularly significant.
items.zh: 他接过许多类似的________，但这一次格外重要。
items.why: 回到对应内容“戈亚以查尔斯四世和皇室1800年的肖像... ...他的职业生涯中最重要的委员会之一... ...完全拒绝皇上，穿着花哨衣服的摩特利”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: This could have been harmful to his career as one court visitor had remarked that the king resembled a ________.
items.zh: 这件事原本可能损害他的事业，因为一位到访宫廷的人曾评论说，国王看上去像个________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“事实上，一位法国游客曾到过西班牙法庭，把查尔斯和他的女王玛丽亚·路易莎比作一个屠夫和他的妻子”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: An 1820 painting of Goya himself shows the artist in old age with a ________ attending to his needs.
items.zh: 一幅作于 1820 年的画描绘了晚年的戈雅本人，有一位________在身边照料他。
items.why: 回到对应内容“在这幅肖像中，这位73岁的画家患有虚弱疾病，并接受医生的照顾”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: This painting is remarkable for its portrayal of the frailty of an ill, older person who is dependent on the ________ of another person.
items.zh: 这幅画的独特之处在于，它刻画了一位年迈病人的虚弱，以及他对另一个人的________的依赖。
items.why: 回到对应内容“如果费迪南代表了人类的尊严戈亚代表了它的脆弱那么阿列塔代表了人类天生的善良”，再按题干要求写出答案。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 升任宫廷画家后，戈雅马上用部分优厚薪水买了马车，随后又写信表达对新地位的自信。
回到对应内容“戈亚以查尔斯四世和皇室1800年的肖像... ...他的职业生涯中最重要的委员会之一... ...完全拒绝皇上，穿着花哨衣服的摩特利”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: His subject was a good one since Goya lived in fascinating times: his lifetime was a period ….
“that saw Spain pass through enormous changes”修饰前面的 period。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 period，再把修饰信息接回主句。

…, they do show types of people – the residents of the city who gave Madrid its street swagger: peasants and rich men, courting couples, singers, hunters, children and young men and women playing blind man's buff or tossing a mannequin into the air.
连接词 although 引出“Although his designs don't show portraits”，说明主句的让步关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 although 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Francisco de Goya, 1746–1828, was a highly-skilled Spanish painter whose portraits can be found in many of the major galleries of the world
弗朗西斯科·德戈亚，1746年至1828年，是一位高度熟练的西班牙画家，其肖像可以在世界许多主要画廊中找到。
vocabulary: 供挂毯织造使用的画稿
